items.title: Harnessing Marvell Accelerators with OVS Hardware Offload for Accelerated Network Performance
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Harman Kalra, Jerin Jacob Kollanukkaran, Marvell

VideoPPTX

Why: Concrete DPU silicon detail (Octeon CN10K) from a vendor other than NVIDIA — useful for anyone comparing offload platforms.

What: An "ovs-offload-engine" alongside OVS that offloads OVS-classified flows into the CN10K's parser/CAM hardware: NIX (controller/DMA), NPC (parser forming MCAM keys, 16K entries), NPA (packet memory pointers), CPT (inline IPsec by intercepting strongSwan SA/SP policies via DPDK rte_security), conntrack-offload compensation, virtio integration up to 100 Gbps, and flow actions (RSS, VLAN strip/insert, mirroring, multicast).

How: Initial/exception packets processed by OVS, then installed into CAM so subsequent packets are matched in hardware; future work includes hierarchical scheduling/shaping up to five levels, LSO, and checksum generation.

Where applicable: Marvell Octeon CN10K-specific; the extracted slides are diagram-heavy and number-light, so treat the performance claims as vendor-stated.
path: Harnessing Marvell Accelerators with OVS Hardware Offload for Accelerated Network Performance

items.title: Improving megaflow cache performance in Open vSwitch with branch prediction
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Wildcard pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Recording

Speakers: Emil Stahl, KTH Royal Institute of Technology; Q&A portion hosted by Eelco Chaudron, Red Hat (from abstract only)

Video

Why: An academic outsider's angle on a practitioner problem — the PM wouldn't search for this, and it may preview where datapath caching goes next.

What: The argument that the slow path (datapath ↔ control plane interaction on megaflow-cache misses) is poised to become the bottleneck in high-throughput networks, and that upcalls can be reduced by predicting imminent traffic — using coflows to anticipate flows before they miss the cache.

How: Benchmarks on an OVN-simulated single-node OCP cluster, with XDP timestamping packets at ingress and egress, driven by synthetic coflow traces with varying flow-size distributions; results analyze how prediction accuracy of varying proportions of future flows affects OVS latency.

Where applicable: Single-node simulation with synthetic traces — research-stage, not production guidance. The idea of predictive cache warming in a vSwitch is the novel hook.
path: Improving megaflow cache performance in Open vSwitch with branch prediction

items.title: Integrating OVN into the Network Fabric
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Felix Huettner, STACKIT GmbH & Co. KG, and Frode Nordahl, Canonical

VideoPDF

Why: The hard boundary between OVN overlays and the physical fabric — stretched L2, MAC-flapping failover, external BGP agents — is a problem anyone running OVN at DC scale hits. This is the most direct fabric/interconnect talk in the program.

What: A rearchitecture of OVN's external connectivity to replace stretched L2 with dynamic routing. A new "magic router" logical construct translates overlay L2 networks into per-chassis point-to-point networks; it is not pinned to any chassis, so egress uses ECMP across gateway chassis and ingress can enter via any of its LRPs. Failover happens by moving dynamic routes instead of MACs, so failover speed is no longer limited by routing convergence, and BFD lets the fabric pick alternate paths.

How: Work in flight includes exporting routes from OVN logical routers to Linux route tables, importing routes back in, auto-generating LRPs/LSPs per chassis (so the CMS needs no changes), and optimizing ingress/egress based on LRP locality. Route advertisement and learning via BGP, with distinct route preferences per gateway chassis and an active-active version of distributed gateway ports. A patchset ("OVN Fabric integration") is on patchwork.

Where applicable: OVN-based clouds generally — the speakers come from STACKIT (OpenStack) and Canonical, and the design supersedes the ovn-bgp-agent pattern. The stretched-L2 drawbacks it enumerates (bonding/MLAG requirements, MAC moves on failover) are universal; the fix requires upstream OVN patches that were not yet merged at talk time.
path: Integrating OVN into the Network Fabric

items.title: Introducing exact-match hardware offload for OVS
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Recording

Speakers: Farhat Ullah, Farhan Tariq, Dreambig Semiconductor Inc. (from abstract only)

Video

Why: Attacks the TCAM orthodoxy in DPU/SmartNIC flow lookup — power consumption and scalability — with an exact-match alternative blending micro/megaflow characteristics.

What: A critique that TCAM-based megaflow offload doesn't scale with ever-growing flow counts, and that TCAM alternatives complicate maintenance and hurt performance as megaflow table counts grow; the proposed solution brings exact-match hardware offload to OVS, demonstrated live.

How / Where applicable: Early-stage, demo-based work from a semiconductor startup; no performance numbers in the abstract. Relevant to anyone modeling DPU lookup-plane power/scalability tradeoffs.
path: Introducing exact-match hardware offload for OVS

items.title: Low on Stack: Flexible protocols vs. Limited Memory
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Ilya Maximets, Red Hat, Inc.

VideoPDF

Why: Deep OVS internals on a real correctness hazard — stack exhaustion from recursive parsing/execution of flexible protocols (Netlink actions, OpenFlow translation) — and it decodes the warnings operators actually see in the field (resubmit limits, deferred action limits).

What: How OVS bounds recursion on both sides of the datapath. Kernel: ~16 kB stack, so nested Netlink actions (e.g., clone(clone(...)), up to 64 kB of nesting in a 16-bit length field) are executed via a Deferred Actions FIFO instead of unbounded recursion. Userspace: 2–8 MB stacks, but OpenFlow translation recurses through goto_table/resubmit/ct(table=N)/patch-port output; the existing depth/resubmit limits work out to roughly 512 B–2 kB of stack budget per rule.

How: The genuinely new technique: track actual stack consumption at runtime using __builtin_frame_address(0) and pthread_attr_getstacksize(), and trigger recirculation when the frame address approaches the stack limit — an RFC patch ("ofproto-dpif-xlate: Recirculate on stack exhaustion") that turns a potential crash into a graceful recirculate-with-frozen-state.

Where applicable: All OVS deployments, kernel and userspace; most acute where controller-generated pipelines (OVN, or any SDN app composing deep resubmit chains) stress translation depth.
path: Low on Stack: Flexible protocols vs. Limited Memory

items.title: ofproto/detrace - The missing link.
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Ales Musil, Dumitru Ceara, Red Hat, Inc.

VideoPDF

Why: The debugging story across OVS/OVN's abstraction layers finally gets a one-command answer — new in OVS 3.4.

What: ofproto/detrace takes a datapath flow's UFID and outputs the OpenFlow rules and groups that contributed to its creation, bridging the gap between optimized kernel flows and the controller-configured pipeline that produced them.

How: The chain is: UFID → OpenFlow cookies → (with ovn-detrace) OVN Southbound Logical_Flows via stage-hints → Northbound objects (Port_Bindings, Load_Balancer VIP mappings, ACLs). The worked example walks a Geneve-encapsulated, DNAT'd connection from dpctl/dump-flows output all the way to the specific load balancer VIP.

Where applicable: Any OVS/OVN deployment on OVS ≥ 3.4; the mantra — "UFIDs → cookies → stage-hints → external-ids" — is worth remembering regardless of tooling.

items.title: Open vSwitch (OVS) performance case study - From software to hardware offloading, from kernel to userspace
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Salem Sol, Gaetan Rivet, NVIDIA

VideoPPTX

Why: The most substantive engineering talk on connection-tracking offload — the feature OVS-DPDK lacks relative to the kernel datapath, and the reason many DPDK-shops still can't fully move off kernel OVS.

What: The implementation history of CT offloads in userspace OVS. A first attempt via rte_flow reused the flow-offload infrastructure but exposed real problems: thousands of offload updates against millions of connections, asynchronous TCP deletion creating a Last-ACK race (a segment acking a FIN could be fully hardware-processed if the offload isn't deleted immediately on FIN), and very short connections actually being slowed by offloading. The rework uses DOCA with a synchronous design: template-based API, pre-allocated pools of match/action/offload resources, static cooperative threads with minimal locking, a mempool of pre-allocated CT offloads with user-configured size, batched offloading, and a dedicated minimal CT table type.

How: Evaluated with CyPerf-generated HTTP traffic comparing OVS-DPDK vs OVS-DOCA: long-connection CPS (30K rate, 850 KB sessions — the favorable case) and short-connection CPS (40K/30K rates, 2 KB sessions — the worst case with ~3 offloaded packets per connection). Claimed outcomes: negligible overhead for short connections, significant improvement for long ones, better scaling/stability under concurrency. (The result charts are images; no specific figures are quotable from the extracted slides.)

Where applicable: NVIDIA hardware via the DOCA framework — vendor-specific. But the design lessons (offload has real per-connection cost; elephant/mice traffic distribution determines whether offloading pays; state synchronization between HW and SW is the hard part) generalize to any CT-offload strategy.
path: Open vSwitch (OVS) performance case study - From software to hardware offloading, from kernel to userspace

items.title: OpenShift Networking Transformed: Fully Embracing DPDK Datapaths in OVN-K8s!
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Jakob Meng, Maxime Coquelin, Red Hat, Inc.

VideoPDF

Why: A complete userspace datapath from NIC to pod in OVN-Kubernetes — kernel bypass inside a managed Kubernetes distribution, with refreshingly honest benchmark results including where it loses.

What: Replaced veth-based pod connectivity with VDUSE (a purely software vDPA device: a kernel driver on the vDPA bus plus a userspace device implemented via the DPDK Vhost library). OVS reuses its dpdkvhostuserclient port type, so the datapath is the well-optimized Vhost-user one; OVN-K8s creates VDUSE devices instead of veth pairs when userspace bridges are detected. Motivations: partitioning (network infra isolated on dedicated CPUs), determinism, and uniformity across primary/secondary networks including KubeVirt.

How: Measured on Intel Xeon Gold 6438N, RHEL 9.6, isolated CPUs, 1 GB hugepages, OVS 3.4+: veth performs slightly better on small block sizes, VDUSE outperforms veth on medium sizes, and VDUSE plateaus on large blocks where ~40% of cycles on the Rx virtqueue IRQ CPU are spent in the bounce-buffer copy (100% busy). Stated cons: memory bandwidth cost from bounce buffers, operational complexity (kernel args, hugepages, NUMA tuning), higher CPU from PMDs (partially mitigated by PMD load-based sleeping at the cost of wakeup latency), and SELinux currently unsupported.

Where applicable: OpenShift/RHEL PoC today (activated by kernel args, prepare-ovs.sh, vfio-pci binding); the VDUSE technique itself is general for K8s clusters wanting partitioned, deterministic pod networking. Preliminary results, explicitly framed as a PoC with upstream productization as future work.
path: OpenShift Networking Transformed: Fully Embracing DPDK Datapaths in OVN-K8s!

items.title: OVS DOCA - The Evolution of hardware acceleration
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Majd Dibbiny, Maor Dickman, NVIDIA

VideoPPTX

Why: Half product pitch, but it contains the cleanest public comparison of OVS's three datapath modes and discloses NVIDIA's upstreaming intent.

What: A mode-by-mode accounting: kernel offload via TC flower (mature, generic, but slow control path, kernel-cycle-bound feature set, can't express dp_hash), OVS-DPDK via rte_flow (kernel bypass, but too low-level, no CT offload, requires cross-vendor consensus), and OVS-DOCA — a DOCA DPIF using DOCA-FLOW with hardware steering claiming 10x+ programming rate, supported with OVN 24.03 and OVN-K8s GA 1.0, based on OVS LTS 3.3.

How: Roadmap items disclosed: upstreaming the DOCA DPIF, live update (Nov 2024 LTS), security acceleration (IPSec and PSP), debuggability, and scale.

Where applicable: NVIDIA hardware; the upstream DOCA DPIF item is the one with community-wide consequences (see Pluggable DPIF).
path: OVS DOCA - The Evolution of hardware acceleration

items.title: P4OVN: Offloading OVN to Intel IPU for Intel Developer Cloud
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Recording

Speakers: Junho Suh, Intel, Inc. (from abstract only)

Video

Why: A production DPU/IPU offload of OVN — not a demo — running in Intel Developer Cloud, and one of the few concrete data points on where SmartNIC-based virtual networking is actually deployed at service scale.

What: A hardware/software co-design: a hardware flow cache implemented in P4 on the IPU's programmable packet processing engine handles L2/L3 forwarding and connection tracking, while the IPU's compute tiles run OVS for stateful processing (ACL, NAT, LB). Covers deployment and operation for distributed virtual routers and distributed/centralized NAT gateways, plus OVN central, engineered to meet IDC scale requirements.

How: Partitioning by statefulness — stateless fast-path classification in programmable hardware, stateful exceptions on the IPU's ARM compute — with an explicit discussion of open-sourcing the work and encompassing other vendors' solutions.

Where applicable: Intel IPU-specific today; interesting as a template for the "programmable-P4 fast path + OVS slow path on DPU compute" pattern that parallels NVIDIA's DOCA DPIF and Marvell's approach.
path: P4OVN: Offloading OVN to Intel IPU for Intel Developer Cloud

items.title: Pluggable DPIF - Unlocking accelerated OVS full potential
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides (PPTX) Slides (PPTX) Recording

Speakers: Roi Dayan, Roni Bar Yanai, Eli Britstein, NVIDIA

VideoPPTX 1PPTX 2

Why: This is the architectural argument for where OVS hardware acceleration is heading — a runtime-pluggable datapath interface — and it comes with the most honest enumeration of why today's "acceleration below the datapath" model is broken.

What: A proposal to make DPIF a loadable, vendor-implemented API (shared object loaded at runtime), so each vendor ships a datapath that co-designs fast path, slow path, and offload — instead of squeezing hardware through TC flower or rte_flow, both of which are too low-level and constrained (no dp_hash, no CT offload in DPDK, vendor match/action mismatches).

How: The slides walk through concrete failure modes of the current model: a ct() action placed mid-pipeline after packet modifications means a HW miss lands in SW with broken context; dp_hash uses Jenkins in SW while HW hashes differ, causing consistency failures and TCP disconnects; meter state split between HW and SW; megaflow aging relying on per-HW-type counters; EMC/SMC cache context invisible to the offload layer. In the proposed model, packets can be bounced back to hardware (with next recirc-id and metadata) to complete the pipeline, and vendors handle their own DPIF maintenance — formalizing what customers already do by forking dpif-netdev.

Where applicable: OVS community architecture decision with ecosystem-wide implications. The reference implementation is NVIDIA's DOCA DPIF, but the proposal is explicitly multi-vendor (P4 vs DOCA Flow cited as different integration styles). Watch this if you have any SmartNIC/DPU strategy.
path: Pluggable DPIF - Unlocking accelerated OVS full potential

items.title: (P)sampling kubernetes network policies
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Dumitru Ceara, Nadia Pinaeva, Adrian Moreno, Red Hat, Inc.

VideoPDF

Why: "Why was this connection allowed or denied" is the top operational pain point in clusters with thousands of NetworkPolicies — and this talk shows the full cross-stack feature chain (kernel → OVS → OVN → ovn-kubernetes) that solves it at line rate.

What: Live NetworkPolicy visibility via OVN ACL sampling (OVN 24.09: new Sampling_App, Sample_Collector, Sample NB tables; per-ACL sample_new/sample_est). It replaces the OVN drop-debugging design's IPFIX export, which forced every sample through the kernel → ovs-vswitchd path, sharing a netlink socket with upcalls (packet loss) and causing IPFIX-cache contention.

How: The kernel's psample netlink multicast group now ships samples directly to listeners, bypassing ovs-vswitchd entirely; OVS gained a psample datapath action (integrated with sample() and trunc(), cookie support added) plus an OVS 3.4 optimization where the sample action's obs_point can be loaded from packet fields (NXM_NX_CT_LABEL). OVN encodes the observation point into ct_label at connection commit, collapsing the reply-direction sampling from O(number-of-ACLs) flows to exactly two flows regardless of ACL count.

Where applicable: OVN-Kubernetes/OpenShift deployments of any size. Note the psample action is implemented in the kernel datapath (ACL sampling itself works with either IPFIX or psample collectors). The pattern — OVN-generated metadata riding packet samples — is extensible to other observability applications.

items.title: Running Open vSwitch on a large CPU System
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Eelco Chaudron, Red Hat, Inc.

VideoPDF

Why: Modern DC hosts are 128–256 CPUs, and this is a rare measured study of what actually breaks in ovs-vswitchd and the kernel datapath at that scale — including an OOM-killer incident reproduced during testing. Directly relevant to anyone running OVS on current-generation EPYC-class compute.

What: On a 128-CPU EPYC 7702P (OVS 3.3, RHEL 9.5), the revalidator process stops scaling past a handful of threads: with 200k datapath flows, mean flow-dump duration goes 169.7 ms → 180.7 ms → 183.4 ms for 4/32/128 revalidator threads, due to lock contention in nl_dump_next() (the mutex serializes netlink dump recvs to avoid an in-kernel EINVAL race on pooled sockets). With traffic landing on many CPUs, per-CPU sw_flow_stat structures (32 bytes each, allocated on demand) consume 782 MB for 200k flows at 128 CPUs and 1.5 GB at 256 CPUs — the real problem is not the memory but the latency of accumulating non-linearly-stored stats, which grows dump duration until a ~1.3 s threshold forces the flow limit down. Interface-statistics sweeps (~every 5 s) take 63 ms at 64 CPUs vs 104 ms at 128, with kernel exception counters adding ~451 ns per interface at 128 CPUs.

How: USDT probes and bpftrace-based scripts (reval_monitor.py, kernel_delay.py), veth/netns test topologies, Scapy traffic pinned with taskset, and 1024-veth-pair configurations to isolate the statistics path. A simulated pod-churn test (128 OVN ports, continuous add/delete) shows ~50% more recvmsg() time at 128 cores, traced toward netdev_get_addrs()/getifaddrs() but left for further investigation.

Where applicable: Kernel datapath (the sw_flow_stat issues are OVS kmod-specific) on large-CPU hosts — K8s nodes, NFV compute. Follow-ups listed: remove the nl_dump_next() mutex, optimize kmod stats gathering, possibly patch glibc's getifaddrs() (which wastes ~6% gathering unneeded per-CPU IPv6 stats).
path: Running Open vSwitch on a large CPU System

items.title: Scalable Multi-Node AI Workloads in Multi-Tenant AI Clouds using SDN K8s Networking
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Leonid Grossman, Girish Moodalbail, NVIDIA (from abstract only; slides link returned 404)

VideoPPTX

Why: AI east-west traffic between GPUs is the newest design driver for vSwitch and fabric requirements — the reason half the offload talks in this program exist.

What: How NVIDIA builds multi-tenant AI cloud networking on OVS/OVN/OVN-Kubernetes: network isolation via overlay virtual network topology, efficient bandwidth via end-to-end QoS, minimizing latency and jitter to prevent GPU underutilization, with much larger gains claimed when OVS-offloadable hardware is used.

items.title: Tracing packets in OVS: an update on Retis
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Paolo Valerio, Adrian Moreno, Red Hat, Inc.

VideoPDF

Why: eBPF-based packet tracing that follows packets across the kernel stack, the OVS datapath, and userspace upcalls — the visibility gap most tools leave.

What: Retis is a network tracing tool where OVS is a first-class citizen: eBPF programs on tracepoints/kprobes plus USDT probes in ovs-vswitchd (requires --enable-usdt-probes) to track a packet from upcall through action execution. New since last cycle: Python bindings (pyo3, on PyPI, with an embedded shell) and OVS flow enrichment — a kretprobe on ovs_flow_tbl_lookup_stats captures the UFID, then Retis queries ovs-vswitchd at runtime via dpctl/get-flow and ofproto/detrace (throttled and cached) to attach the full datapath and OpenFlow flows to trace events.

How: Event series show a single curl packet with its conntrack NAT actions annotated inline; limitations honestly stated (no reliable tracking of flow deletion/update, upcall flows not displayable).

Where applicable: Linux + OVS kernel datapath debugging; valuable for anyone who has tried to answer "what did OVS do to this packet" with tcpdump and failed.
path: Tracing packets in OVS: an update on Retis

items.title: VM Migration Enhancements
items.text:
Digest: Open vSwitch and OVN 2024 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 20–21 November 2024

Abstract Slides Recording

Speakers: Naveen Yerramneni, Nutanix (contributors: Naveen Yerramneni, Shibir Basak, Mansi Sharma, Nutanix)

VideoPPTX

Why: Live migration is where overlay networking semantics visibly break (proxy-ARP races, FDB staleness, conntrack loss) — and these are real upstream OVN features, not Nutanix-private patches.

What: New logical switch port options for migration: pkt_clone_type=mc_unknown (clone traffic to unknown ports while the destination binding is being established, fixing drops at migration start), disable_arp_nd_rsp (skip the ARP/ND responder so packets reach the port instead of being eaten by stale proxy ARP on the source), force_fdb_lookup (learn a port's additional MACs through OVN's native FDB, avoiding packet duplication when combined with cloning), and disable_garp_rarp. Plus FDB cleanup on port down, and controller CT-zone reservation (external_ids:reserve_ct_zones) so conntrack entries can be synchronized during migration — the latter two patches under review at talk time.

How: Each option targets a specific drop scenario demonstrated across a VXLAN-extended subnet spanning availability zones.

Where applicable: OVN generally (upstream options); the cross-AZ migration topology is Nutanix's use case, but the failure modes are universal to any live migration over OVN.

items.title: A native way of integrating OVN into the fabric through BGP-EVPN.
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Ales Musil (Red Hat), Dumitru Ceara (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: OVN deployments have historically been islands attached to the physical fabric through gateways or external controllers. With native BGP in 25.03 and experimental BGP-EVPN in 25.09, OVN logical L2 domains now stretch directly into and across the DC fabric — the concrete mechanism by which the overlay joins the EVPN fabric.
  • What: OVN-native EVPN support: a provider logical switch's L2 domain is extended across an IP fabric via VXLAN, with the BGP-EVPN control plane (run by FRR) distributing MAC/IP (type-2) and, planned for 26.03, type-5 routes. OVN learns remote VTEPs, remote FDBs, remote IPs (with ARP suppression) and remote routes; it advertises local workload MACs/IPs, connected networks and NAT IPs back into the fabric. L2 EVPN is implemented and experimental in 25.09; L3 EVPN per-VRF is the 26.03 plan.
  • How: The CMS pre-configures br-$vni / lo-$vni / vxlan-$vni interfaces in the default network namespace; OVN monitors FRR/zebra state via NetLink and programs the OVS datapath: per-VTEP OpenFlow cookies on br-int, tun_id/tun_src/tun_dst loads, learn() actions with 30s hard timeouts for dynamic FDBs, and ARP-suppression flows on logical routers. Configuration is per logical switch via dynamic-routing-vni plus ovn-evpn-local-ip.
  • Where applicable: Any OVN deployment needing L2/L3 fabric extension; datapath-agnostic (OVS kernel or DPDK) and hardware-offload friendly since VXLAN is terminated in OVS. Constraints: at most one local IP per EVPN tunnel today, fixed host-side interface naming (fine-grain naming is an open question), needs FRR on OVN nodes, and it is explicitly experimental with the authors soliciting design feedback.
path: A native way of integrating OVN into the fabric through BGP-EVPN.

items.title: A Nightmare on Kube Street: Slicing Kubernetes Networks like Freddy Krueger
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Dave Tucker (Red Hat), Surya Seetharaman (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: Kubernetes multi-tenant isolation is still flat; this talk brings cloud-provider VPC semantics to OVN-Kubernetes on top of User-Defined Networks — policy at the network-topology level rather than per-pod NetworkPolicy.
  • What: A concept mapping of VPC constructs across AWS/Azure/GCP/VMware/OpenStack onto OVN-K8s (UDN = subnet, NetworkPolicy = security groups, OVN routers = route tables/T0-T1 gateways), then a new ClusterNetworkConnect CR: a group of label-selected UDNs/cluster networks connected via shared supernet CIDRs (connectSubnets per address family with networkPrefix), with explicit connectivity grants (PodNetwork, ClusterIPServiceNetwork). Working prototype demonstrated.
  • How: Label-based networkSelectors match UDNs/CUDNs; east-west traffic runs over Geneve, north-south SNATs pod IPs to node IPs; OVN logical switches/routers/policies provide the segmentation.
  • Where applicable: OVN-Kubernetes clusters needing self-service team networks with platform-team-controlled inter-network communication. Prototype-stage, but with clear forward hooks already named: RouteAdvertisements (BGP), EVPN to provider networks, and cloud-construct integration.
path: A Nightmare on Kube Street: Slicing Kubernetes Networks like Freddy Krueger

items.title: AI-Powered Performance Insights: Integrating OVS/OVN automatic performance regression analysis with LLMs
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Wildcard pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Joe Talerico (Red Hat), Jose Castillo Lema (Red Hat), Mohit Sheth (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: Shows how performance engineering for Kubernetes networking is being automated and made LLM-queryable — shift-left performance testing operating at real scale, with coverage numbers rather than claims.
  • What: Red Hat Perf&Scale's continuous performance testing: benchmarks (k8s-netperf, ingress-perf, cluster-density-v2) run against PRs early; Orion, a Python library doing automated statistical regression detection (Apache Otava e-divisive change-point detection) over an Elastic/OpenSearch data warehouse; and Orion-MCP, an MCP server that lets LLMs answer "has my PR regressed OpenShift?", correlate regressions with PR changelogs, and surface version-tagged results (OVN, OVN-K, OVS versions per run). Scale: 5 platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP, IBM, bare metal, plus ROSA/ARO), 100+ weekly tests; 2025 added net-new workloads for UDN L2/L3, Virt UDN, NetworkPolicy, EgressIP and BGP, with 30+ downstream bugs filed.
  • How: Fingerprint-based result retrieval (platform, node types/counts, benchmark, networkType: OVNKubernetes), change-point detection on the matched series, and MCP tool calls surfaced through Slack (GitHub integration next). Next steps: agentic AI for CPT and pushing a perf workload into ovn-ci upstream.
  • Where applicable: OpenShift/OVN-Kubernetes development workflow; Red Hat-internal tooling, but the Orion + Orion-MCP pattern is directly replicable by any team with a benchmark data warehouse.
path: AI-Powered Performance Insights: Integrating OVS/OVN automatic performance regression analysis with LLMs

items.title: Baremetal network isolation for cloud providers with OVN on DPUs
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Adrian Chiris (NVIDIA), Mael Kimmerlin (NVIDIA), Tarek Abu-Hariri (NVIDIA)

VideoPPTX

  • Why: Secure multi-tenancy for bare-metal cloud nodes without per-tenant switch configuration — the DPU is the enforcement point a tenant cannot reach even with privileged host processes. Combines the PM's physical DC and network security interests, and it ships real throughput numbers.
  • What: OVN/OVS offloaded to BlueField-3 and run in a separate trust domain under cloud-admin control; tenant VPCs (bridged L2 networks with DHCP, masquerade, external routing, floating-IP-class features) enforced transparently to the host, with declarative Kubernetes CRDs (DPUVPC, DPUVirtualNetwork, DPUServiceInterface) mapping bare-metal machines to tenants dynamically. Test results: node-to-node RoCE with Geneve encapsulation on BF3 with 2×200Gb/s links — 191.9 Gb/s without ECMP, 383 Gb/s with ECMP (BGP to an L3 ToR, single hop, OVS-based HBN router).
  • How: An OVN logical structure modeled on OVN-Kubernetes, optimized for bandwidth and few hops; isolation at the PF/VF level; ECMP via BGP; HBN (host-based networking) OVS router on the DPU.
  • Where applicable: NVIDIA BlueField-3-specific. Roadmap includes OVN-IC, BGP-EVPN integration (replacing the external router with OVN BGP), SFC, and nested OVNs; the multi-tenancy API is currently admin-only. Real numbers, but from the vendor's own testbed.
path: Baremetal network isolation for cloud providers with OVN on DPUs

items.title: Beam Me Through the Datapath: VDUSE for OpenShift Virtualization
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Jakob Meng (Red Hat), Maxime Coquelin (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: Completes a fully-userspace datapath (OVS-DPDK + VDUSE) for KubeVirt VMs, with unusually transparent benchmarking that includes cases where DPDK loses to the kernel datapath.
  • What: Extends last year's container userspace work to VMs via VDUSE/vhost-vDPA (primary and secondary networks), plus new workload-partitioning knobs in OpenShift (strict-cpu-reservation, dedicated CPUSet, irqbalanceBanned, static PMD masks). Benchmarks (Xeon Silver 4310, CX-6 Dx, OVS 3.5+): OVS-kernel outperforms OVS-DPDK on large TCP buffers; small-buffer throughput improves with pmd-sleep-max (~90,000 → ~3,000 IRQs/s, QEMU 200% → 115% CPU at 128B buffers) at the cost of large-buffer performance; a virtio-net IRQ-coalescing prototype in the DPDK vhost library fixes that without sleeps. Also documents CX-6 Dx lacking outer-UDP checksum offload (which forced software segmentation — tying into the checksum-offload revamp) and KubeVirt's fixed 256-descriptor virtio rings.
  • How: VDUSE is a purely software vDPA device implemented by a userspace application (the OVS DPDK vhost backend), attached through the vDPA bus; vhost-vDPA serves QEMU.
  • Where applicable: OpenShift Virtualization, telco and real-time use cases. Preliminary results, explicitly framed as transparent benchmarks; the partitioning APIs are OpenShift-specific but the datapath work is upstream OVS/DPDK.
path: Beam Me Through the Datapath: VDUSE for OpenShift Virtualization

items.title: Multiple NICs as Encapsulation Endpoints for Large Scale GPU Cloud
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Girish Moodalbail (NVIDIA), Han Zhou (NVIDIA)

VideoPDF

  • Why: In GPU servers each GPU typically has a dedicated NIC (4 GPUs = 4 NICs), so inter-node AI training traffic is multi-homed and each NIC's IP becomes an encapsulation endpoint — while vanilla OVN assumes one encap IP per chassis. This is the scaling problem AI clouds are hitting right now, and it lands squarely in physical DC / scale territory.
  • What: Multi-NIC encap endpoint support in OVN/OVN-Kubernetes: per-VIF selection of source/destination encapsulation IPs, full-mesh tunnels (all local × all remote encap IPs), new flow programming using an Encap-ID in REG13[16..31], and host-side routing fixes for both the kernel and OVS-DPDK paths. Special cases are handled: distributed gateway ports (skip pinning or fall back to default encap) and ovn-ic transit-switch ports (proposal: multiple TS-LR ports plus /32 routes and a new request-encap-ip).
  • How: ovn-encap-ip carries a comma-separated IP list; per-interface encap-ip external_ids drive Port_Binding:Encap in the SB DB, populated by ovn-controller. The kernel path needs source-based policy routing plus rp_filter/arp_ignore/arp_announce sysctls; the DPDK path required an upstreamed OVS multi-table routing fix (ovs-router). Egress flows scale O(E×P) — local encap IPs × remote port bindings.
  • Where applicable: Demonstrated on NVIDIA GPU cloud / cloud gaming topologies, but the mechanism is generic OVN. Scale is the open issue: 8 NICs × 1000 chassis ≈ 64k tunnel ports per node, which stresses ovs-vswitchd. Mitigations proposed but not yet landed: flow-based tunnels (loses IPSec/BFD), a "Transport Plane" grouping that cuts 64→8 tunnels per node (87.5% fewer), and intra-node tunneling to preserve HW offload across NICs.
path: Multiple NICs as Encapsulation Endpoints for Large Scale GPU Cloud

items.title: Observing Open vSwitch with native prometheus metrics
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Gaetan Rivet (NVIDIA)

VideoPDF

  • Why: OVS observability today depends on external exporters that assume the kernel datapath and scrape CLIs; a native exporter unifies kernel and userspace observability with lower footprint — practical for anyone running OVS at scale.
  • What: A Prometheus-compatible metrics framework inside the OVS library: counter/gauge/histogram types, and a per-process metrics tree whose internal nodes mirror module structure (datapath cache/conntrack/offloads, interfaces, memory, ofproto). Node types cover subsystems, labeled collections (FOREACH), bounded collections for label generation, and conditionals (e.g., offload metrics only when hw-offload is on). Exposed via an ovs-exporter systemd service (default port 6103), ovs-appctl metrics/show, and Python bindings; new metrics appear automatically without new CLI plumbing.
  • How: The tree is statically defined (API in lib/metrics.h), interpreted at scrape time, and rendered into the Prometheus text model — the design is deliberately output-format-agnostic so other formats could follow.
  • Where applicable: OVS kernel and userspace datapaths alike; initial coverage: resource consumption, interface counters and link state, ofproto upcalls/revalidation, and coverage counters. Complements (rather than competes with) DOCA-Telemetry on NVIDIA kit.
path: Observing Open vSwitch with native prometheus metrics

items.title: OpenFlow Classifier: Arcane knowledge and common pitfalls
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Ilya Maximets (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: The classifier is the hottest path in OVS and determines megaflow quality, which drives datapath autonomy and flow-cache effectiveness. Understanding its subtable model explains OVN pipeline performance and recent regressions and fixes — core datapath-internals material, delivered by a current maintainer.
  • What: A deep dive: rules are grouped by match pattern into per-mask hash "subtables"; lookup iterates subtables ordered by the highest priority they contain; complexity is O(1) per subtable hit and O(n) over distinct masks. "Un-wildcarding" produces the megaflow mask — false 1-bits are allowed but degrade caching; false 0-bits are correctness bugs. Optimizations covered: staged lookup (the mask split into 4 segments with early exit, sharply reducing un-wildcarded bits for non-matching packets) and prefix tracking. Pitfalls: mask explosion from many distinct match patterns, and historically from OVN's inequality matches (single-bit masks, fixed October 2025 to use prefixes; IPv6 address pairs can still theoretically yield 128×128 masks).
  • How: Practical do/don't guidance for OpenFlow pipeline authors: match earlier-stage fields alongside later ones where logic permits, never let struct flow dependencies cross segment boundaries, and avoid generating fragmented masks.
  • Where applicable: Every OVS deployment; especially relevant to OVN logical-flow generation and anyone reading megaflow traces.
path: OpenFlow Classifier: Arcane knowledge and common pitfalls

items.title: OVN-Kubernetes Meets DPUs: Enabling Service Function Chaining and Shared OVN
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Tim Rozet (NVIDIA)

VideoPDF

  • Why: Shows concretely how DPU adoption is driving new OVN features — SFC and "Shared OVN" — i.e., where the OVN architecture is heading for offloaded security/auditing pipelines, with an explicit call for contributors.
  • What: An SFC design for OVN (RFC 7665 semantics): initially SFC-unaware service functions (no NSH), using Geneve to carry chain metadata between nodes; a new Service_Function_Chain NB table with two modes — local (no conntrack, allows packet modification, all SFs on one chassis, symmetry requires an explicit reverse chain) and immutable-global (conntrack-implied symmetry, chain can cross nodes, no packet modification); Network_Function_Group gains a load-balance mode for multiple SF instances. Shared OVN: one OVN instance serving multiple CMSs — one per DPU plus one for the host cluster — with RBAC separation.
  • How: A two-cluster DPU model (Kubernetes running on the DPU) lets DPU admins enforce security at the edge by injecting SFC classifiers as ACLs into the host cluster's traffic; open questions stated plainly — is OVN RBAC secure enough for this, and does shared OVN actually reduce resource consumption?
  • Where applicable: OVN-Kubernetes on BlueField-class DPUs; enhancement proposal under active discussion (June 2025 ovs-dev thread); single-cluster SFC targeted first, shared two-cluster second.
path: OVN-Kubernetes Meets DPUs: Enabling Service Function Chaining and Shared OVN

items.title: OvS and Socket Maps - Beyond ports as endpoints
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Wildcard pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Aaron Conole (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: A genuinely surprising datapath idea: treat application sockets as packet endpoints and skip the IP stack entirely. Measured ~1000ns of 7395ns per-packet protocol overhead in netns-to-netns forwarding — relevant to anyone watching eBPF/XDP-style bypass techniques reach general SDN tooling.
  • What: An exploration with four prototype approaches (in-datapath table, userspace-centric, eBPF-based, plus a socket-map variant), with numbers: 7395 → 6190ns per packet (and ~23k more 65k-packets/s) using a sock(try) action to skip conntrack; the socket-map-style approach measured 8254ns — essentially identical to plain output, reported without spin. Difficulty is candidly labeled "very much a nightmare": tracking sockets across netns boundaries and rewriting recirc state. Preliminary patches are posted; the direction is undecided.
  • How: OVS already knows the destination socket from tuple/conntrack state; sock() actions would enqueue directly to application sockets, skipping L3 routing and re-parsing inside the target netns, while trying to preserve OVS's flow-centric (megaflow) semantics.
  • Where applicable: OVS kernel datapath with local (same-host) endpoints; experimental RFC stage (June 2025 ovs-dev thread). The eBPF variant is described as the most future-proof but hardest to integrate with OVS userspace.
path: OvS and Socket Maps - Beyond ports as endpoints

items.title: OVS-DOCA live-upgrade
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Eli Britstein (NVIDIA)

VideoPPTX

  • Why: Upgrading ovs-vswitchd in production today means a full daemon restart — losing conntrack state (dropping TCP sessions), FDB, meters, groups, TLV-map, configured routes, and tunnel neighbor tables, plus re-initializing ports with offloads. A zero-downtime model matters for any DC or carrier SLA.
  • What: OVS-DOCA achieves in-place upgrades by starting the new version in client mode alongside the running server: the server keeps forwarding while the new instance initializes ports and offloads in parallel; volatile state is migrated to the new instance; then a zero-time handover and server termination. Version and resource constraints, failure handling, and rollback are addressed.
  • How: DOCA can initialize the same ports from different userspace processes and hand over between them with zero interruption.
  • Where applicable: OVS-DOCA (NVIDIA's downstream OVS) on ConnectX/BlueField — not upstream OVS today. The state-migration problem it solves, however, is universal for production OVS. (from abstract only; the slide deck could not be extracted and the program page adds nothing beyond the abstract)

items.title: OVS-DOCA upstream roadmap
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Maor Dickman (NVIDIA)

VideoPPTX

  • Why: Signals where hardware offload in upstream OVS is heading: NVIDIA is moving DOCA acceleration from a downstream fork into upstream via the dpif-netdev framework, which means new upstream OVS APIs (dpif-offload-provider, userspace CT offload).
  • What: The plan: a new netdev_doca netdev class (port initialization and software slow path under dpif-netdev), a new dpif-offload-doca provider (offloading megaflows, based on a new dpif-offload-provider API), and a new connection-tracking offload API for the userspace datapath. Gaps are acknowledged: eswitch hierarchy (one port handling all device ports), port-init ordering, partial offload (HW-to-SW miss path), and advanced offloads (sFLOW, tunnel entropy, meters, DP_HASH). This replaces the earlier dpif-netlink-based DPIF-DOCA direction.
  • How: Staged upstreaming steps are enumerated: offload-provider first, then the netdev, then dpif-offload-doca, then agreement on the CT offload API. DPIF-DOCA will live as a standalone open-source library while DOCA-Flow/DOCA-Eth remain closed-source.
  • Where applicable: ConnectX/BlueField with the OVS userspace datapath. Vendor roadmap — but with concrete architectural consequences for upstream OVS; watch the dpif-offload-provider and CT-offload API discussions if you care about offload in OVS.

items.title: Programming OVS bridges using OVN Bridge Controller
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Numan Siddique (Crusoe AI)

VideoPDF

  • Why: New in OVN 26.03 (merged the week before the conference): program any OVS bridge using OVN logical-flow syntax instead of raw OpenFlow — motivated by a real end user (Crusoe) that needed to program provider bridges after the OVN pipeline.
  • What: ovn-br-controller plus a new OVN Bridge OVSDB database; the CMS writes logical flows (bridge, table, priority, match, actions) and the controller compiles them to OpenFlow exactly as ovn-controller programs br-int. It injects physical mapping flows (loading interface ofports into registers, a NORMAL fallback) and translates logical actions into concrete rules; multiple bridges per host are supported.
  • How: Per-hypervisor services started via ovn-ctl; external_ids:ovn-br-remote points the controller at the ovnbr DB; an ovn-brctl CLI handles bridge and flow creation.
  • Where applicable: Anyone programming provider/physical bridges on top of OVN-based stacks. Current limitations are stated: no restriction against adding br-int, and OVN-specific controller actions (put_dhcp_opts, put_fdb) are not yet restricted; incremental processing and code-sharing with ovn-controller are future work.
path: Programming OVS bridges using OVN Bridge Controller

items.title: Revisiting checksum offloads in OVS
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

David Marchand (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: The userspace (DPDK) datapath's checksum/TSO API had grown buggy and tightly coupled to DPDK; this is a full revamp with per-NIC performance numbers — directly relevant to high-throughput OVS on real hardware.
  • What: The OVS 3.6 redesign: a new dp_packet::offloads field with four-state (unknown/bad/good/partial) Rx statuses for IP and L4, tunnel encapsulation expressed as status metadata, and TSO reduced to a tso_segsz value. Massively expanded unit tests caught real bugs (simple-match checksums, IPv6 UDP, conntrack ICMP-embedded checksums, IP fragmentation handling). OVS 3.7 adds an outer-UDP-checksum optimization: for valid inner IPv4/TCP, the outer UDP checksum equals the inner checksum sum, so it can be derived rather than computed — plus "partial segmentation" so HW TSO packets can use it.
  • How: Inner/outer statuses split via a 16-bit shift; netdev drivers (netdev-dpdk) translate OVS statuses into mbuf Tx flags, isolating OVS core from DPDK/kernel APIs. Measured on mlx5 CX-6 Dx: Geneve TCP 6.08 → 7.31 Gbit/s from the outer-UDP optimization, and 7.3 → 10.4 Gbit/s at 37% CPU once HW TSO works; comparative numbers across CX-6 Dx, X710 and E810, including which NICs lack outer UDP checksum offload entirely.
  • Where applicable: OVS userspace/DPDK datapath; behavior is NIC-specific and the feature is still marked experimental (the talk asks whether to change that). The CX-6 Dx gap found here directly feeds the VDUSE talk's benchmark findings.

items.title: Space - building a CMS with OVN Concepts
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Felix Huettner (StackIt)

VideoPDF

  • Why: An end-user case study of a cloud provider whose requirements (policy-based routing combined with dynamic routing, deny ACLs, per-ACL logging) outgrew Neutron — and who, rather than replacing OVN, built a custom CMS layer on OVN design concepts.
  • What: "spaced", a Go daemon using ovn-kubernetes' libovsdb, translating a custom "spacebound" OVSDB schema into the standard OVN northbound DB — effectively a custom northd. It coexists with Neutron through per-table resource ownership (either Neutron or spaced writes a given NB table), with a full migration off Neutron as the long-term goal.
  • How: Sticks to OVN's layered model (NB/SB/northd/ovn-controller), inserting spaced between the CMS and NB; the processing engine is modeled on OVN's incremental-processing engine (not yet implemented). Challenges listed honestly: libovsdb is event-driven with no consistent-state reads, no automatic reference resolution, and no change tracking.
  • Where applicable: StackIT / Schwarz Digits' OpenStack+OVN production environment — org-specific, but a useful template for anyone considering building a CMS directly on OVN primitives instead of adopting a full CMS.
path: Space - building a CMS with OVN Concepts

items.title: The BGP Fork in the Road: A Tale of Two Implementations
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Jaime Caamaño Ruiz (Red Hat), Patryk Diak (Red Hat), Surya Seetharaman (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: Two BGP implementations were built in parallel — OVN's native dynamic routing and OVN-Kubernetes' FRR-k8s integration — and whether they converge determines how K8s clusters exchange routes with the provider network. BGP internals are squarely in the PM's interest set.
  • What: A side-by-side anatomy. OVN: BGP-daemon-agnostic ("bring your own FRR"), routes exchanged through kernel VRFs over NetLink, with Advertised_Route / Learned_Route tables in the OVN DB; by default the VRF carries control-plane traffic only and the host routing table is untouched; dynamic-routing-vrf-id frees the VRF table ID from the datapath tunnel key. OVN-Kubernetes: a RouteAdvertisements CR generates FRRConfiguration for FRR-k8s; in Local Gateway mode a VRF is in the data plane, in Shared Gateway mode BGP-learned routes are copied into OVN gateway routers. Then the gap list for adopting OVN's native BGP: table-ID collisions, distinct vs shared VRFs, default VRF support, filtered learning, real next hops instead of blackhole routes, and per-LSP/per-LB /32 advertisement.
  • How: Concrete merge path proposed: CMS-managed table IDs (already landed in controller/northd), shared VRFs as the more efficient but harder option needing extra OVN support (filtered learning, actual next hops on advertised routes).
  • Where applicable: OVN-Kubernetes / OpenShift clusters peering with provider networks. The merge is a proposal, not a done deal — this is an honest gap analysis, not an announcement.
path: The BGP Fork in the Road: A Tale of Two Implementations

items.title: Transit router - The distributed router for OVN interconnect.
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Ales Musil (Red Hat), Mairtin O'Loingsigh (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: OVN interconnect (ovn-ic) previously offered only a Transit Switch; there was no simple way to route between Availability Zones. The Transit Router fills that gap as a distributed logical router spanning AZs — and it already underpins the OVN-Kubernetes Layer2 re-architecture (see the upgrade talk below).
  • What: A logical router instantiated across AZs in an ovn-ic deployment, behaving like OVN's distributed routers; new ovn-ic-nbctl verbs (tr-add, trp-add, trp-del, tr-list); per-AZ ARP learning with ARP responses flooded between AZs via specially added flows. The deck includes a full packet-level walkthrough (SNAT on the gateway router, Geneve tunnels between chassis, lr_in_ip_routing flow selection).
  • How: tr-add allocates a unique datapath tunnel key, delegates the ICSB datapath binding, and creates a router in each AZ; trp-add assigns resource allocation per AZ, creates logical router ports, and syncs port binding tunnel keys.
  • Where applicable: Multi-AZ OVN interconnect deployments, generic OVN. Open questions acknowledged: definition and synchronization of routes and route rules across the TR, and "local" TRP port semantics.
path: Transit router - The distributed router for OVN interconnect.

items.title: Turbocharge Kubernetes with offloaded OVN-Kubernetes and OVS on DPUs
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Adjacent pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Alin Serdean (NVIDIA), Amit Zala (NVIDIA), Mael Kimmerlin (NVIDIA), Igal Tsoiref (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: A production-oriented, DPU-offloaded Kubernetes platform (DPF) with benchmark numbers — and a notable strategic shift: OVN-Kubernetes is moving upstream-first, reviving DPU-host mode after roughly two years dormant.
  • What: DPF (DOCA Platform Framework) manages DPU fleets declaratively: DPUSet provisioning (BFB images), DPUService/DPUServiceChain lifecycle via ArgoCD, version-compatibility gating, and rollout-velocity budgets; service chaining runs an OpenFlow controller patch-paneling OVS ports on the DPU; OVN-Kubernetes runs in DPU mode with hardware acceleration for workload pods alongside HBN. Measured 354.92 Gbit/s iperf3 between pods across two BF3 nodes through HBN plus the service chain. Future work: OVN-K as the DPU cluster's primary CNI (dropping Flannel), 2+ OVN-K instances per host, RDMA-accelerated traffic in OpenShift, and selective pod offloading instead of "offload everything".
  • How: Two-cluster model — host cluster plus DPU clusters run as HyperShift hosted control planes; RHCOS brought to BlueField via a custom coreos-installer flow; the SC CNI stamps DPF service metadata onto OVS ports so the chaining controller can create patch-panel rules.
  • Where applicable: NVIDIA BlueField-3 + OpenShift. Treat the numbers as vendor-reported (some slides were marked NVIDIA confidential) — but the OVN-Kubernetes upstream-first shift, DPU-host-mode revival, and the OpenShift integration challenges (CNO, security model, RHCOS) are genuine engineering signal.
path: Turbocharge Kubernetes with offloaded OVN-Kubernetes and OVS on DPUs

items.title: Virtual Network Function integration in OVN
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Sragdhara Datta Chaudhuri (Nutanix), Naveen Yerramneni (Nutanix)

VideoPPTX

  • Why: Inserting third-party firewalls / network functions into the OVN traffic path has been a long-standing gap; this is a concrete, code-in-review design for bump-in-the-wire service insertion — network security chaining at the OVN layer.
  • What: ACL-matched traffic is steered through a VNF's port pair (inline mode) or cloned to the VNF (tap mode); stateful symmetry via conntrack labels; VNF groups with datapath-probe health monitoring; member selection or load balancing across healthy members; configurable fail-close vs fail-open when all members are unhealthy; enforced tunneling for cross-host traffic to and from the VNF's node. Supports active/standby now, active/active planned.
  • How: New logical-switch pipeline stages, new NB entities for network functions, a new ACL action, a new ovn-controller health-monitor type; conntrack labels redirect response packets and enforce tunnel behavior.
  • Where applicable: OVN with either VLAN or overlay subnets, vendor-agnostic VNFs. Status: patch series in code review (July 2025 on ovs-dev). Note: the slide deck is mostly diagrams with no extractable detail, so this write-up is grounded in the abstract only.
path: Virtual Network Function integration in OVN

items.title: When CI Shouts Back: LLMs in the OVS CI Pipeline
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Wildcard pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Aaron Conole (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: Not networking — but a clear signal of where core infrastructure projects are heading: LLM-assisted code review inside the OVS CI pipeline, with the friction reported honestly rather than sold.
  • What: Experiments with CodeRabbit, Sourcery, and Claude SONNET-class models on OVS patch review. Findings: PR-based bot workflows fragment patch discussion into a second venue, branches must be kept very tightly in sync, and bots contradict themselves between runs ("suggest doing one thing then doing another"). A custom Claude-based reviewer (RFC on patchwork) offers own prompts, developer-runnable execution, and GitHub Actions integration — at real dollar cost.
  • How: PW-CI infrastructure changes plus custom prompting instead of SaaS review bots.
  • Where applicable: OVS CI specifically, but the lessons (bot consistency, cost, review-venue splitting) generalize to any patch-based OSS project evaluating review bots.
path: When CI Shouts Back: LLMs in the OVS CI Pipeline

items.title: You Want to Upgrade WHAT? A Field Guide to Risky Network Changes
items.text:
OVS + OVN 2025 Fall Conference (Prague) digest Core pick Prague · 19–20 November 2025

Abstract Slides Recording

Nadia Pinaeva (NVIDIA), Dumitru Ceara (Red Hat), Patryk Diak (Red Hat)

VideoPDF

  • Why: A rare, detailed production migration narrative: OVN-Kubernetes' legacy Layer2 UDN topology was redesigned around the OVN Transit Router while customers ran on it, with real failure modes and fixes documented — exactly the incident-detail-rich content worth a PM's time.
  • What: The legacy L2 topology (node-specific gateway routers) broke VM live migration (stale ARP for the migrated gateway MAC; IPv6 RAs from multiple node gateways creating broken multipath defaults, worked around by iptables-blocking external RAs in every L2 pod), doubled maintenance for each new feature, and forced EgressIP hacks. The new topology makes a transit router the network's default gateway with the same IP and MAC on every node. The bulk of the talk walks the rolling upgrade through a half-old/half-new cluster, including hand-crafted routes and dummy IPs to bridge old and new gateway routers during the mixed state, and hand-crafted route advertisements to flush stale routes.
  • How: Rolling per-node upgrade rewires topology while workloads are drained and rebooted; NAT moves through the transit router; explicit static routes (e.g., 100.65.0.2 via 100.88.0.5) stitch the two topologies together.
  • Where applicable: OVN-Kubernetes Layer2 UDNs in production; the authors note it is based on actual joint debugging sessions across the OVN and OVN-Kubernetes communities. The migration playbook generalizes to any non-disruptive OVN topology change.
path: You Want to Upgrade WHAT? A Field Guide to Risky Network Changes

items.title: Agentic DDoS OPS/AI-Powered Operations Layer for GenieATM
items.text:
Peering Days 2026 digest Wildcard pick 25 March 2026

Slides

Siarhei Matashuk, Genie Networks

PDF

  • Why: Not optics, not BGP — it's an early, concrete look at how LLM agents get wired into live NOC operations, and the design patterns (git-versioned markdown skills, a hard privacy boundary, an earned-autonomy trust model) generalize far beyond DDoS tooling, including into the identity and authorization questions agentic systems raise for the PM's own portfolio.
  • What: An agent layer ("DjiNN") on top of GenieATM implementing nine virtual NOC/SOC roles as "skills" — Baseline Analyst (continuous detection-threshold tuning with auto-rollback, replacing set-and-forget thresholds), Traffic Analyst (natural-language queries over a 1M-flow in-memory snapshot, e.g., breakdown of a new uplink by origin ASN/protocol with no query syntax), Peering Coordinator (cross-referencing per-AS traffic against PeeringDB to surface peering ROI, e.g., "40% of traffic to AS 13335 rides transit but they're at AMS-IX where you already peer, est. €2,400/month savings"), plus Incident Responder, Platform SRE, and others clearly staged as MVP vs Phase ⅔. Notably honest limitations: LLM latency handled by rule-based fallback for time-critical detection (the LLM does enrichment, not first-trigger); trust via a maturity model from L0 alert-only to L3 autonomous-with-audit-trail, with all destructive actions human-approved; data privacy via an MCP anonymization layer (IP→prefix_UUID, Router→router_XXX) so only tokenized data crosses to the LLM provider, with a local-model option for zero exposure.
  • How: Skills are plain ~30-line .md job descriptions in git — a NOC engineer can read and modify one in five minutes, no SDK; an orchestrator routes tasks → skills → tools → data sources; southbound to GenieATM's Snapshot API/NetFlow plus PeeringDB, RIPE RIS, RouteViews, and threat intel.
  • Where applicable: The data source is GenieATM-specific and the closing slide recruits for an early-access program (vendor session — discount accordingly), but the skill-file architecture, trust maturity model, and anonymization boundary are platform-agnostic patterns worth borrowing.
path: Agentic DDoS OPS/AI-Powered Operations Layer for GenieATM

items.title: Demystifying Coherent Optics for Network Professionals
items.text:
Peering Days 2026 digest Core pick 25 March 2026

Slides

Marcin Bala, Salumanus

PDF

  • Why: Coherent pluggables (100ZR, 400G ZR/ZR+/ZR++, 800G ZR/ZR+) are collapsing the router-to-DWDM boundary and changing DC/WAN interconnect economics — squarely the PM's physical-optics territory. This is a working engineer's guide, not a marketing deck.
  • What: A market/standards map (OIF 400ZR/800ZR, OpenZR+, CMIS) and a four-step deployment method: link requirements (length, dark fiber vs DWDM, grid, OSNR, throughput) → transceiver selection → matching application to link budget → configuration. Worked examples: a 200 km DWDM link on a 50 GHz grid at 19 dB OSNR served by either QSFP28 100ZR or QSFP-DD OpenZR+ ZR100-OFEC-QPSK; a 21 dB/100 GHz path running ZR300-OFEC-8QAM with 3x100GbE host-side, or ZR++ to keep 400GbE host-side; an 18 dB flex-grid path forcing ZR200-OFEC-QPSK or an 800G module in ZR400-OFEC-QPSK (150 GHz passband). Also covers the 400G-to-100G interconnect case via muxponder (75 GHz spectrum instead of 200 GHz, future-ready for direct 400G optics), and SFF modules emulating QSFP28 LR4/LR1/DWDM2 for CMIS-less legacy gear.
  • How: Concrete CLI on four platforms — Juniper (optics-options application mediaid/hostid, tx-power, wavelength), Nokia (optics-profile 400ZR, dwdm coherent target-power, frequency), Cisco (zrp-optics fec oFEC muxponder …), OcNOS (qsfp-dd application, laser grid/fine-tune). Parameter guidance: OSNR ~24 dB for 400G 16QAM vs ~16 dB for 200G QPSK; Q-factor >8 dB good, 6.5–8 monitor, <6.5 failure risk. Common failure modes: mismatched host/media applications between ends, mismatched channel number, ignored optical budget.
  • Where applicable: Broadly applicable — open OIF/OpenZR+ standards, multi-vendor config. Speaker is an optics vendor CTO, but the content is standards- and config-centric, with deployment mistakes/checklists rather than product claims.
path: Demystifying Coherent Optics for Network Professionals

items.title: EVPN - One control plane to rule them all
items.text:
Peering Days 2026 digest Core pick 25 March 2026

Slides

Patrick Prangl, Arista Networks

PDF

  • Why: Consolidating all L2/L3 VPN service delivery onto one BGP control plane across DC and WAN is exactly the PM's DC/WAN interconnect space, and this maps the RFC landscape, the SR-MPLS→SRv6 migration tiers, and the gateway designs that make it real.
  • What: The case for EVPN as the single service control plane: EVPN-VPWS (RFC 8214) for E-LINE, EVPN-L2VPN (RFC 7432) for E-LAN, EVPN-L3VPN Type-5 (RFC 9136), and EVPN multicast (RFC 9625 OISM) — replacing LDP/BGP-VPLS, MC-LAG, Draft-Rosen/NG-MVPN, and per-service signaling protocols. Transport strategy: SR-MPLS reusing existing MPLS hardware and BGP control plane (TI-LFA for 50 ms FRR, FlexAlgo for controller-less macro-TE, controller-based micro-TE), with three SRv6 maturity tiers — SR-MPLSv4 (no hardware change), SR-MPLSv6 (IPv6 forwarding plane, possible HW upgrade), SRv6 uSID (likely HW upgrade, new control plane). EVPN gateway design per BESS RFCs/drafts (8365, 9014, draft-ietf-bess-evpn-ipvpn-interworking): VXLAN↔MPLS interworking where Type-⅖ routes are re-advertised across domains with re-encapsulation while Type-⅓/4 stay local; gateway next-hop chaining so leaves only learn local next-hops; D-PATH attribute for inter-domain loop prevention. Forward-looking pieces: Unknown MAC Route (MAC=0 + gateway ESI) to bound MAC scale in multi-domain fabrics, and the multicast gateway family (MEG, PEG, EEG).
  • How: One BGP AFI/SAFI across all service types; gateways translate encapsulation and own inter-domain next-hop re-advertisement, containing control-plane state per domain; D-PATH domain-ID tagging prevents route loops across gateway meshes.
  • Where applicable: Explicitly covers greenfield build-outs and brownfield MPLS/SR coexistence with interop gateways; transport per use case (VXLAN in DC/campus, MPLS-SR/SRv6 in WAN, VXLAN-over-IPSec for SD-WAN). Arista vendor session, but anchored in IETF standards — the architecture applies to multi-vendor EVPN deployments.
path: EVPN - One control plane to rule them all
